subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: When a legacy BLOB key and TEXT key normalize to the same canonical STRICT primary key but may carry different payloads, should migration fail safely and preserve the source database, or should OpenClaw define a documented reconciliation rule?
rationale: The canonical STRICT table cannot retain two rows with the same normalized primary key, and choosing a winner is persisted-data policy rather than a mechanical type conversion.

options.title: Fail safely on canonical-key conflicts
options.body: Detect conflicts before insertion, preserve the legacy database unchanged, and surface a recoverable diagnostic until an explicit repair policy exists.

options.title: Define a reconciliation contract
options.body: Specify which fields and provenance determine a merged or winning row, then implement it with migration fixtures proving no meaningful state is lost.

options.title: Accept current deletion behavior
options.body: Keep the TEXT-row preference and explicitly accept that a legacy collision can discard the other row’s state.

recommendation.title: Fail safely on canonical-key conflicts
recommendation.body: Detect conflicts before insertion, preserve the legacy database unchanged, and surface a recoverable diagnostic until an explicit repair policy exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision extends the STRICT migration behavior introduced by the SQLite safety work.
